content:
Apple's September was already quite exciting, but they appear ready to carry that momentum into October, with several long-awaited products potentially on the way.

#1: MacBook Pro / Ultra with Touchscreen and New Design

The Mac has long resisted adding a touchscreen, but that may finally be about to change — rumours suggest Apple will unveil an all-new MacBook Pro (or MacBook Ultra) in October.

Apple's next-generation MacBook Pro will feature a completely new industrial design, the first major revamp in five years. Beyond adding touch capability, it will also sport an OLED display, Dynamic Island, and may offer an optional C2 cellular modem.

The MacBook Pro hasn't had a fresh look for a long time, and the wait for a touchscreen has been even longer — but Apple has consistently chosen not to bring this feature to the Mac. I'm looking forward to seeing how touch functionality eventually enhances the Mac experience.

#2: All-New Apple TV 4K

The Apple TV hardware has never gone this long without an update. Apple's current newest model is the third-generation Apple TV 4K, launched in 2022.

Rumour has it we may finally see a brand-new Apple TV 4K in October, with the focus on a powerful A19 or A19 Pro processor, as well as support for Siri AI features.

Apple raised prices on most of its products this summer, and the Apple TV was no exception. This means the already four-year-old Apple TV 4K now costs US$199 — well above its original US$129 launch price. I sincerely hope the new Apple TV won't cost even more.

#3: "HomePad"

Rumours about a HomePod with a screen have been around almost as long as the HomePod itself. But such reports intensified in 2024, when Mark Gurman published an in-depth report about a product widely referred to as the "HomePad".

Billy Coker's comment received the most likes

Honestly, I'm genuinely tired of Apple TV articles until the product actually launches. Always "coming soon," "coming soon" — but never actually arriving.

HomePad is a smart display with a built-in speaker, reportedly set to lead Apple's re-entry into the smart home market. It will run a brand-new operating system with an interface blending elements of iOS, tvOS, and watchOS, including a StandBy-like mode.

Siri AI is expected to be central to this product, which will also feature a camera, customisable widgets, and built-in Apple apps including Photos, Notes, Music, and Calendar.

Which upcoming Apple product are you most looking forward to, whether launching in October or later? Let us know in the comments.
